I bought my house in 2019 right before Covid when interest rates were creeping up. Got a 4.3% rate locked in, no down payment, and no PMI since I had excellent credit and no debt. I almost re-financed during Covid because interest rates bottomed out and I could have locked in a 2-2.5% interest rate but was too lazy to go through the closing process again. 

Even though I got a 30 year mortgage I had already decided beforehand that I wasn't going to simply pay the minimum mortgage payment each month. Racking up all of that interest would have sickened me lol.  Instead I've been treating it like a 10 year mortgage and making a hefty extra payment toward the principal every month. In 3 years I'll have the house paid off and it'll be a major asset since the home value has only gone up. With today's housing market I can see why people would pass on buying a house. I got in at the right time and dodged that bullet.
